name: Dual-tree plumbing mirror - byte-exact, never merges
description: Blueprint 91 of 96 (design BP-REL-05). Mirror blobs between two trees that must stay in sync using git PLUMBING only, so smudge/clean filters, EOL conversion and working-tree state cannot change the bytes. Mechanism: blob-hash identity. It writes ONLY where the target blob is unchanged relative to the last mirrored state; any path where BOTH sides changed is REPORTED for a real merge and never written. This is deliberately a subworkflow - it is the reusable deterministic primitive that live-to-repo-drift-reconcile calls, and it contains no agent judgement at all.

source_tree.description: ABSOLUTE path to the tree that is authoritative for the mirrored paths

target_tree.description: ABSOLUTE path to the tree receiving the mirror

path_map.description: Explicit source->target path pairs. There is no glob expansion: an implicit path set is how a mirror acquires a path nobody agreed to.

normalize_eol_before_compare.description: Compare LF-normalised content so a CRLF-only difference is classified EOL-ONLY instead of drift. The WRITE is still byte-exact from the source blob.

baseline_ref.description: The ref (or note) recording the last mirrored blob per path. Without it, 'target unchanged' is unknowable and every one-sided change looks safe to overwrite.

mirror-executor.description: Executes plumbing commands and compares hashes. It has no discretion: every decision is a hash comparison.

merge-owner.description: Receives the divergent-path report. This workflow never merges; it hands the two-sided changes to whoever owns them.

stages.title: Compare blob hashes, separating EOL-only from real drift

work_unit.title: Hash both sides of every mapped path and classify identical / eol-only / source-ahead / target-ahead / two-sided
work_unit.question_or_target: For every pair in path_map read the SOURCE blob with `git cat-file -p <rev>:<path>` and the TARGET blob the same way, plus the baseline blob from baseline_ref. Classify into IDENTICAL, EOL-ONLY, SOURCE-AHEAD (target == baseline), TARGET-AHEAD (source == baseline), TWO-SIDED (neither equals baseline). Never use `git archive` - on this box it applies export-time EOL conversion and returns CRLF where cat-file returns LF.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: byte comparison is answerable by an exact algorithm; handing it to agents measured 86% accurate with 100% of the errors pointing at data loss (fan-out-contract C4)

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per path the three blob hashes (source, target, baseline) and the derived class; a class with no hashes behind it cannot be re-derived and is not evidence
tests_required: a pair differing only in line endings must be classed EOL-ONLY, not drift
a pair where both sides differ from baseline must be classed TWO-SIDED

both-states control: a control fixture using `git archive` instead of `git cat-file` must produce a DIFFERENT byte count for the same path, proving the transport choice is load-bearing rather than stylistic
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none - the classification is a hash comparison and any reader can re-run it; the reviewer requirement attaches to the TWO-SIDED report, which a human merges
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9101 emitted only when every mapped path carries three hashes and exactly one class; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9101 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry on a classification mismatch - a hash that changes between two reads means the tree is being written concurrently, which is a FAILED terminal state, not a flake

stages.title: A working-tree copy applies filters and changes bytes
Write ONLY the paths where the target is still at baseline

work_unit.title: Write one source blob into the target index by hash and re-read it
work_unit.question_or_target: For one SOURCE-AHEAD path: `git hash-object -w` the source blob into the target object store, `git update-index --cacheinfo` it at the target path, then read it back with `git cat-file -p` and assert the hash is identical to the source hash.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a plumbing write plus a hash assertion

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the pre-write source hash and the post-write re-read hash for this path, plus the literal plumbing command lines used
tests_required: a write whose re-read hash differs must FAIL rather than report success
no working-tree checkout command may appear in the recorded command lines
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none - the re-read hash is the reviewer; a mismatch is a hard failure
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9102 emitted only when the post-write re-read hash equals the source hash; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9102 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry only if the failure class is object-store-lock; never retry a hash mismatch, which means the bytes changed in transit

stages.title: A mirror that did not re-hash did not verify anything
Two-sided changes are reported, never written

work_unit.title: Emit the divergent-path report for the paths this workflow refuses to touch
work_unit.question_or_target: List every TWO-SIDED and TARGET-AHEAD path with both sides' hashes and a one-line description of what each side uniquely holds, and state explicitly that none of them were written. Name the owner who must merge them.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the CLASSIFICATION is mechanical, but describing what each side uniquely holds is exactly the judgement a differ cannot do - so only that description is modelled

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per divergent path both hashes plus the specific lines each side holds uniquely; a bare 'both changed' verdict does not tell the merger what is at stake
tests_required: a TWO-SIDED path must appear in this report AND be absent from the write receipts - the two artifacts together are the proof that nothing was overwritten
both-states control: a one-directional check that only asks 'does the source have extra content' must be shown to MISS a two-sided case that the bidirectional check catches
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the named merge owner reads it; this workflow does not resolve divergence and must not claim to
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9103 emitted only when every non-mirrored path is enumerated with both hashes and the write receipts contain none of them; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9103 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - the report is derived from artifacts already on disk, so a failure means an artifact is missing

estimate.measurement_source: 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md#BP-REL-05 - a prior measurement over the skill vault found 19+ files whose only difference was line endings, i.e. a large false-drift category that EOL normalisation removes

impact.blast_radius: writes blobs into the target object store and index for SOURCE-AHEAD paths only; every write records the pre-write hash, so each is individually revertible

derived_from.credit: owner - `git archive` returns CRLF here while `git cat-file` returns the blob

x_extensions.mechanism: blob-hash identity against a recorded baseline. Five classes, one write rule: write ONLY where target == baseline. It has no merge capability by construction, which is what makes it safe to call from another workflow.

not_a_duplicate_because.vs_live-to-repo-drift-reconcile: that workflow DISTRUSTS a specific sync tool and gates on a both-states control before it will run at all, then routes CHANGED files to a human two-directional merge. This one has no tool to distrust and no merge path: it CALLS OUT rather than merges. The reconcile workflow declares this document in its subworkflows block and delegates the deterministic half to it, so the classification logic exists once, not twice.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_anchor-checked-per-file-deploy: that writes into a target that is KNOWN to be divergent, using a content anchor as the precondition and a symbol assertion as the postcondition. This refuses to write a divergent target at all.

contraindications: NOT when the two trees SHOULD diverge
NOT as a substitute for a merge when both sides changed - that is precisely the case it refuses

benchmark_cases.given: the same content stored CRLF on one side and LF on the other
benchmark_cases.expect: class EOL-ONLY, and the write is still byte-exact from the source blob

benchmark_cases.given: a path where source and target both differ from baseline
benchmark_cases.expect: present in divergent-paths.json, absent from write-receipts.json

benchmark_cases.given: one file read via `git archive` and via `git cat-file` on this box
benchmark_cases.expect: a byte-count DIFFERENCE, proving the transport is load-bearing (measured: 3,837 vs 3,737 bytes, 100 CRLF vs 0)

worked_examples.terminal_state: SUCCESS:BPW-9103 - 0 writes, 1 path reported for merge, 1 EOL-only reclassified out of drift
worked_examples.note: Zero writes is a SUCCESS here. The value delivered is that one file was correctly withheld from an overwrite and one false-drift entry was removed - which is the outcome the design predicts, not a no-op.

unverified: The EOL-only category size on this estate is UNVERIFIED at 19+ files - that figure comes from a prior measurement quoted in the design card, not from a run of this workflow. Settling experiment = run stage classify-by-blob-hash over the full skill-vault path map and count EOL-ONLY against real drift.
